  "screen_decision": "exclude",
  "screen_rationale": "The study uses physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling, which is an in silico method, to extrapolate methylprednisolone pharmacokinetics from animals to humans. It does not report a quantitative measure of agreement between whole-animal in vivo results and human clinical results, such as a concordance rate or translation rate. Instead, it focuses on modeling and prediction.",
  "arm": "safety-pharmacology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study models methylprednisolone pharmacokinetics, which is relevant to safety pharmacology due to its use in managing inflammation and its pharmacokinetic properties.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "sepsis-inflammation",
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Methylprednisolone is used to manage inflammation, and the study's pharmacokinetic modeling is applicable across species, suggesting a cross-cutting relevance.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study utilizes physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models, which are computational models, and extrapolates across multiple species.",
  "species": [
    "rat",
    "multiple-aggregated"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study digitized plasma profiles and PK parameters in 7 species and specifically mentions PBPK results in rats, extrapolating from rats to humans.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study focuses on pharmacokinetic parameters like clearance (CL) and volume of distribution (Vd), which are biomarkers of drug disposition rather than hard clinical outcomes."
